The most compelling feature is the very large proportion of necrosis (62.04%), which is a hallmark of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype. Additionally, the presence of thick-walled contrast enhancement, extensive infiltration across the midline (a 'butterfly' pattern), and invasion into deep white matter and deep gray nuclei are all classic radiological signs of an IDH-wildtype glioma. There are no significant features to suggest an IDH-mutant tumor, which typically presents with less necrosis and more circumscribed margins.

The large, centrally necrotic, and infiltrative mass crossing the corpus callosum ('butterfly glioma') is a classic presentation. All radiological features consistently point towards this high-grade diagnosis with very high confidence.
